EEX013.summary: Vṛdhnaśva offers wealth, but Agastya declines because the king’s income equals his expenditure; Vṛdhnaśva then joins Agastya and Śrutarvan in visiting Trasadasyu.

TEX_008.note: Mahadevan paraphrases Puṟanāṉūṟu 201 and separately proposes identifying the unnamed sage as Agastya. The poem itself and its translation have not been independently checked here.

TEX_006.note: The Tamil prologue names Agastya’s overturned vessel and the river’s emergence. The crow occurs in Hart’s explanatory English prose, not in the cited Tamil lines.

REX006.note: Cowell’s English for the second half of 4.73 is difficult; this records co-mention only, without inferring kinship or a second event.

VEX004.note: “Sons of Māna” is in 1.171.5. The identification of Māna as Agastya’s father is commentary. Do not merge him automatically with a Māna in RV 7.33.

TF010.subject: tamil_adipathi
TF010.summary: After Brahmadarman’s warning, King Adipathi orders his people to leave and travels north with his army toward Avanthi.

TF016.subject: tamil_buddha_peedihai
TF016.summary: The Buddha Peedihai foretells the heroine’s rebirth under the name Kavera Kanni.
TF016.note: The shrine, not the goddess Maṇimēkalai, is credited with the prediction.

TF017.note: Kavera Kanni is a predicted name for the heroine in the rebirth account, not counted as a second distinct individual.

TF024.summary: Aṟavaṇar tells Lakshmi about the Buddha’s sacred footprints and invites her to worship them.

TF025.subject: tamil_madhavi
TF025.summary: The goddess says Mādhavi is the rebirth of Thārai.

TF026.subject: tamil_sudhamathi
TF026.summary: The goddess says Sudhamathi is the rebirth of Vīrai.

GSM011.subject: vp19_bhavanmanyu
GSM011.summary: Vitatha, also called Bharadvāja in this translation, is the father of Bhavanmanyu.

GSM040.subject: vp19_para_samara
GSM040.summary: Pāra, son of Samara, is the father of Pṛthu in this branch.

GSK031.note: The verse-indexed Sanskrit witness distinguishes Saudāsa and his son Sahadeva. ANU English reads “Saudāsa Sahadeva” as one expression; retain the witness variant rather than treating both readings as one settled genealogy.

GSK032.note: This follows the Sanskrit witness’s Saudāsa → Sahadeva → Somaka sequence; ANU English punctuation/wording differs.

ANU18_038.summary: The childless Aṅga-line Daśaratha receives Śāntā as a daughter from Aja’s son Daśaratha.
ANU18_038.note: The passage says she was given to him; it does not describe a formal adoption rite.

GKA023.subject: vp20_parjanya
GKA023.summary: Parjanya sends rain during Śāṃtanu’s reign after Devāpi is deemed ineligible to rule.

GKA041.summary: Dhṛtarāṣṭra has sons with Gāndhārī; the passage identifies their parentage without narrating the marriage.

GKA087.summary: Abhimanyu is the father of the later Parīkṣit born to Uttarā.

TL051.note: The speaking goddess image represents the previously named Kaṇṇaki; the image is a separate graph node, not a second counted person.

GFK001.note: This is Abhimanyu’s son Parīkṣit and his future son, distinct from Kuru’s earlier Parīkṣit and Janamejaya in chapter 20.

GFK002.note: Future son of Abhimanyu’s son Parīkṣit; distinct from the same-named son of Kuru’s earlier Parīkṣit.

GFK003.note: Future son of Abhimanyu’s son Parīkṣit; distinct from the same-named son of Kuru’s earlier Parīkṣit.

GFK004.note: Future son of Abhimanyu’s son Parīkṣit; distinct from the same-named son of Kuru’s earlier Parīkṣit.

TFNL003.summary: The Alavaivādi names Saimini among the three sages followed by his Vaidika tradition while speaking to Maṇimēkalai.

TFNL012.summary: A Brahmavādi says to the heroine that Brahmā created the worlds.

TFNL013.summary: A Vaiṣṇava interlocutor tells the heroine that Nārāyaṇa protects the world.
